fibroblast adhesions to the substratum are mediated by fibronectins and that these adhesions are formed in stages that involve the externalization of matrix proteins from the cell.

fibronectins (both exogenous and endogenous) play a part in the adhesion, locomotion and growth of fibroblastic cells, but are not obligatory for the formation or maintenance of the adhesive structure, which may be stabilized by other extracellular matrix components.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of cell-substratum interactions, the nature and roles of the adhesive structures that are formed, and the relationships of these to other cellular structures and functions.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the adhesions and locomotion of primary chick fibroblasts involve the interaction of the cells with the extracellular matrix, in which both exogenously and endogenously derived fibronectin are implicated, and that the formation of the adhesions involves a sequence of stages, some of which involve the externalization of cell-derived fibronectin.
the formation of focal contacts is a complex, multi-step process involving the interaction of a number of cell surface molecules with the extracellular matrix.
fibronectins are not essential for the formation of adhesion, but are required for the development of the mature structure, and are involved in the expression of the adhesion function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
adhesions are formed by the interaction of the cell with its substratum and that this interaction involves both exogenous and endogenous fibronectins.

fibroblasts can adhere to substratum and locomote on substrata of a variety of proteins, but the development of the adhesive structure, and its subsequent maturation into a focal adhesion, is a complex process involving both exogenous and endogenous fibronectins, as well as laminin.

fibroblasts can form adhesions and spread on substrata in a variety of ways, depending on the nature of the substrate, the source of the extracellular fibronectin, and the availability of the cellular fibronectins.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the formation and maintenance of focal adhesion complexes is an important part of the process that regulates the adhesion and spreading of fibroblastic cells and that this regulation is mediated through the expression of extracellular matrix proteins.

the adhesive structure that is formed between a cell and its substratum is a dynamic one and that the cell is capable of modifying its adhesive properties as a function of its state of differentiation and its interactions with other cells.
the adhesive structures that mediate cell adhesion and motility are dynamic and that the adhesive structures are formed in a stepwise manner.
